name: Japhia
overview: Japhia was a male king who ruled over the city of Lachish during the Israelite conquest of the Promised Land. He is specifically identified as the King of Lachish in the biblical account recorded in Joshua 10:3. Beyond his royal title and role in this conflict, Scripture does not provide additional details about his tribe or family background.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Japhia' is a proper name that may mean 'may the deity shine,' reflecting a possible theistic hope or blessing. His title, 'King of Lachish,' clearly identifies his political authority over the city of Lachish during the conquest period. Neither name is indicated as being divinely given.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Japhia beyond his role as King of Lachish. No additional familial connections or relationships are noted in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Japhia's significance lies in his position as a local ruler resisting the Israelite conquest of Canaan. As King of Lachish, he represents one of the city-states opposing Israel's divinely commanded takeover of the land. His mention in Joshua 10:3 situates him within the broader narrative of God's fulfillment of His promise to give the land to Israel through conquest under Joshua's leadership.
